businessRules.text: On create (POST), the spec's `CdrTransaction_FVO` requires `@type`, `channel`, `relatedParty` and `transactionItem` to be present, each with their own nested mandatory sub-fields (`channel.channel.id`, `relatedParty.partyOrPartyRole.id`, `transactionItem.cdr.productRef.id`, etc.) — see the userguide's "Mandatory Attributes" table for the full list.
`href`, `id`, `@baseType`, `@schemaLocation` and `@type` are immutable and must be rejected on PATCH.
`cancellationDate` / `cancellationReason` are only meaningful once the transaction has been cancelled; they are not implied by any other field.
`requestedInitialState` only records the client's requested initial state; the authoritative current state is always `state`.

Four notification events are declared by the spec (`Create`, `AttributeValueChange`, `Delete`, `StateChange`), but `StateChange` should only actually fire when `state` is present in the resource — `CdrTransaction` has no `lifecycleStatus`, so the generator's conditional-mandatory-column rule already keeps `lifecycleStatus` out of the schema.
